Bill.BriefDescription: Implementing linear K-3 class size reductions.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to linear K3 class size reduction; amending RCW28A.150.260; adding a new section to chapter 28A.525 RCW; creating anew section; making an appropriation; and providing an expiration date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature intends to provide adetailed plan to foster cooperation with the Washington supreme courtby placing into statute a roadmap for steady forward progress toimplement the basic education K3 class size reduction to seventeenstudents by 2018. The legislature also intends to provide additionalnonbasic education funds to assist with capital costs for schooldistricts that have facility capacity limitations in meeting the targetof reducing class size to seventeen.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28A.525RCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Notwithstanding other provisions in law, beginning in the2014-15 school year through the 201718 school year, as the stateimplements K3 class size reduction in accordance with RCW 28A.150.260,school districts that do not have sufficient facility capacity toimplement the K3 class size reduction may apply to the superintendentof public instruction for state assistance to modernize existing schoolfacilities, provide portable or modular buildings or classrooms, or tofacilitate new construction to implement K3 class size reduction. Tobe eligible for state assistance under this section a school districtmust demonstrate the following: (a) The existence of unhoused K3 students, which for the purposeof this section means current or projected enrolled students who are in p. 9 SB 6108excess of the capacity calculated for existing facilities within thedistrict to implement the K3 class size reduction under RCW28A.150.260; and (b) The ability of the district to obtain capital funds to providethe local share required for state funding assistance, except fordistricts that do not have bond or levy capacity or have failed a bondor levy ballot measure that focused on facilities for K3 class sizereduction. (2) The school facilities citizen advisory panel created under RCW28A.525.025 shall review all applications and make recommendationsregarding the state assistance under this section to the superintendentof public instruction based on the kind and extent of the school plantfacilities required, the urgency of need for the facilities in theschool district seeking state assistance, and the ability of the schooldistrict to provide other available educational space in the schooldistrict that could be used for the K3 class size reduction. (3) The office of the superintendent of public instruction shalladopt rules to implement this section. (4) This section expires July 1, 2020.

The sum of two hundred fortyone million onehundred fortyone thousand four hundred dollars, or as much thereof asmay be necessary, is appropriated for the fiscal year ending June 30,2015, from the general fund to the office of the superintendent ofpublic instruction for the purposes of section 3 of this act.
